Done. The merged, sharded checkpoint is in `out/T5/`, produced by a single execution of `out/T5/solution.py`.

**Approach.** A plain safetensors plus torch script. It pairs each adapter `lora_A`/`lora_B` with its base tensor by stripping the `base_model.model.` prefix, computes `2 * (B @ A).T` in float32 and adds it to the Conv1D weight, then packs tensors greedily into shards of at most 100 MiB of tensor data and writes the index file. All four required checks run before writing, and a post-write reload re-verifies the tensor set and shard budgets.

**Result.**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Executions | 1, succeeded |
| Adapter pairs merged | 12 |
| Tensors written | 160 in 5 shards |
| Unchanged tensors bit-exact with base | 148 |
| Relative Frobenius error vs PEFT merge_and_unload | 0 on all 12 layers |

**One pitfall worth noting.** Running PEFT's own merge on `GPT2LMHeadModel` silently merges nothing, because the adapter keys lack the `transformer.` prefix. Loading `GPT2Model` instead needs the CAUSAL_LM task type dropped. I used PEFT only as an independent cross-check, not as the solution, and recorded this in the report.

**Files.** `out/T5/solution.py`, `out/T5/REPORT.md`, five shard files, and `out/T5/model.safetensors.index.json`.
